title: Canonical left compact-support compositors: coefficient, refinement and shift coherence
statement: For the constructible coefficient systems of [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients] and the canonical finite and integral maps of [def-sf-finite-exceptional-compositor-maps], composable separated finite-type maps between separated quasi-compact finite-type schemes over the algebraic closure of a finite field admit three such systems and a family of LeftCompositors [def-sf-exceptional-compositor-coefficient-data]. Its finite and integral components equal finiteAlpha and integralAlpha, its rational and common components satisfy the fixed coefficient equations, all components commute with their specified integer shifts, and the family commutes with the recorded compactification refinement comparisons. The normalization uses the fixed operation package [lem-sf-package-compactified-tower-comparisons].

source.place: Complement: composition law and mate; geometric left composition/coherence supplied by sk-thm-sf-comp-composition and the operation package, as expanded in the assigned parent node proof Steps 1, 5 and 6.

proof.text: Choose the three normalized coefficient systems using [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients]. Lift the finite and completed compact-support compositors through the full finite-Tor inclusions, retaining precisely finiteAlpha and integralAlpha. The completed realization equality is constructibleIntegralSupport_eq of [def-sf-constructible-exceptional-compositor-data].

The normalized tower comparison and its horizontal and vertical pasting identities give the left refinement square. Total derived limit of equal strict maps preserves this square; no faithfulness of derived finite-level evaluation is used.

Finite structural-map shift compatibility gives the finite equation. Apply integral realization shift coherence to each finite word with a common Tor and cohomological interval to obtain the integral equation.

Extend the integral maps to raw rational Hom modules by linearity and tensor generation; then descend compatible common-field representatives. Coefficient normalization and refinement/shift squares pass through these operations.

lean.statement:
theorem constructibleLeftCompositorCoherence
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} (B : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (S : ∀ (E : FieldStage.{u} B.l) (n : ℕ+),
      SixFunctorOperationDatum D B E.carrier n n.pos)
    {X Y Z : SixFunctorSpace D}
    [IsSeparated X.obj.hom] [IsSeparated Y.obj.hom] [IsSeparated Z.obj.hom]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [IsSeparated f.hom.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.hom.left] [QuasiCompact f.hom.left]
    [IsSeparated g.hom.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType g.hom.left] [QuasiCompact g.hom.left] :
    ∃ (P : System B.l B.Qbar D B.different (f := f.hom.left))
      (Q : System B.l B.Qbar D B.different (f := g.hom.left))
      (R : System B.l B.Qbar D B.different (f := (f ≫ g).hom.left))
      (A : LeftCompositors B f g P Q R S),
      (∀ (cf : Compactification f.hom.left) (cg : Compactification g.hom.left)
        (cx : Compactification (f ≫ g).hom.left) (s : Stage.{u} B.l),
        (A.alpha cf cg cx s).hom.CommShift ℤ) ∧
      (∀ (cf df : Compactification f.hom.left) (rf : cf.Refinement df)
        (cg dg : Compactification g.hom.left) (rg : cg.Refinement dg)
        (cx dx : Compactification (f ≫ g).hom.left) (rx : cx.Refinement dx)
        (s : Stage.{u} B.l),
        (A.alpha cf cg cx s).hom ≫ (R.refinements.refinement rx s).left.hom =
          Functor.whiskerLeft (P.ring.operation cf s).F
            (Q.refinements.refinement rg s).left.hom ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight (P.refinements.refinement rf s).left.hom
            (Q.ring.operation dg s).F ≫ (A.alpha df dg dx s).hom)
